children: Lindt said Chief Executive Officer Adalbert Lechner will leave the company, as the chocolatier makes a sweeping overhaul of leadership in a bid to return to growth.
The Swiss chocolate company said Lechner would depart after 33 years at the firm. Lechner didn't immediately reply to a request for comment.

The board initiated a search process to find a successor, while Vice-Chairman and former CEO Dieter Weisskopf will take on the role on an interim basis. Weisskopf previously led Lindt as CEO for six years, until 2022.
"My task is to hand over to the next CEO a company with renewed momentum," said Weisskopf, adding that profitability is a priority.

Lindt said the board had concluded that it needed new leadership to bring consistent growth. Also on Monday, it said Michal Spiller, the CEO for Germany, would depart the company and the current Austria CEO Ali Kulein would take his place.

Known for its gold Easter chocolate bunnies and colorful eggs, the company has grappled with lackluster volumes, price-sensitive consumers and volatile cocoa prices. Shares have slumped around 25.3% this year to Friday's close.

Lindt slashed its outlook twice this year, citing lower-than-expected order volumes. Initially, it gave annual targets of 6% to 8% organic sales growth for 2026, and later capped the range at 4%. In September, it updated expectations to have flat sales to 2% growth for the year.
It recently cited struggles with order volumes in Germany, Switzerland and Austria, and a particular pullback in its seasonal businesses, which include Easter and Christmas.
The broad leadership reset indicates that there were different internal views on European pricing, sensitivity, and how quickly corrective action was needed, Vontobel's Jean-Philippe Bertschy said.
